title: Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk
wikitext: {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk | image = Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk.jpg | caption = Mykhailiuk with the Ukraine U16 team, in 2012 | number = 10 | position = [[Shooting guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 8 | weight_lbs = 212 | league = | team = | nationality = Ukrainian | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1997|6|10}} | birth_place = [[Cherkasy]], Ukraine | college = [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] (2014–2018) | career_start = 2012 | career_end = 2014 | years1 = 2012–2014 | team1 = [[Cherkaski Mavpy]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2018) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2014) }} '''Sviatoslav "Svi" Mykhailiuk''' ({{lang-uk|Святосла́в Михайлю́к}}, {{IPA-uk|sʋʲɑtɔˈslɑu̯ mɪxɑjˈlʲuk|pron}}; born June 10, 1997) is a Ukrainian [[basketball]] player who most recently played at the [[University of Kansas]]. He played for [[Cherkaski Mavpy]] in the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]] from 2012 to 2014. He also played for the Ukrainian national team in the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Cherkasy]], [[Ukraine]], Mykhailiuk's mother, Inna, a high school biology teacher, and his father, Yuriy, a college history professor.Dodd, Rustin. [http://www.kansascity.com/2014/05/21/5037687/ukrainian-teenager-sviatoslav.html Ukrainian teenager Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk signs to play for KU basketball team], ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', May 22, 2014.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2014/may/21/sources-ukrainian-wing-mykhailiuk-chooses-ku/?mens_basketball Ukrainian wing Mykhailiuk chooses KU], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', May 21, 2014 He attended high school at Cherkasy First City Gymnasia. ==Ukrainian national team== Mykhailiuk played for the Ukrainian under-20 national team in the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] in [[Helsinki]].{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=July 17, 2016 |title=Mykhailiuk unloads for 14 in U-20 tourney |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/jul/17/mykhailiuk-unloads-14-u-20-tourney/?mens_basketball |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=July 18, 2016}}{{cite news |last= |first= |date= |title=Junior Male Team (U20) |url=http://fbu.ua/national-team/team-621/ |newspaper=[[Ukrainian Basketball Federation]] |location=[[Kiev, Ukraine]] |access-date=July 18, 2016 |language=Ukrainian}}{{cite news |last= |first= |date=July 17, 2016 |title=Game Story |url=http://www.fiba.com/europe/u20/2016/1707/Ukraine-Serbia#tab=game_story |newspaper=FIBA |location=[[Mies]], [[Switzerland]] |access-date=July 18, 2016 }} During the tournament Mykhailiuk led his team in scoring at 14.9 points per game in seven tourney games.{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=July 25, 2016|title=Mykhailiuk scores 21 in final loss |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/jul/25/mykhailiuk-scores-21-final-loss/?mens_basketball |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=July 25, 2016}} He hit 36.8% of his floor shots. Mykhailiuk shot 47.2% from two and 19% from three point territory. He made 85.7% of his free throws and also grabbed 5.6 rebounds a game with 2.7 assists and 4.7 turnovers with 2.1 steals per game. Mykhailiuk played for the Ukrainian national team, which competed at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], in [[Spain]] August 30 to September 14.{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=August 25, 2014 |title=Chillin’ out: ‘Svi’ excused from Challenge |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2014/aug/25/chillin-out-svi-excused-challenge/ |newspaper=Lawrence Journal-World |location=Lawrence, Kansas |publisher=The World Company |accessdate=August 25, 2014 }} In the summer of 2013 he played with the Ukrainian national team in the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]. He was selected in the All-Tournament Team,fiba.com [http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/coid_kG7Aj2BgG76iJfEHEBQN,2.articleMode_on.html 2013 U16 All-Tournament Team] after completing an outstanding championship, averaging 25.2 points, 8.0 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game.fiba.com [http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/cid_z8jOMILgHCsbXTL1wG4sq0.teamID_2183.compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2013.roundID_9441.playerID_99106.html Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk 2013 U16 stats] ==College career== Mykhailiuk received offers from [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite news |last=Saat |first=James |date=February 18, 2015 |title=The American Dream |url=http://contentviewer.adobe.com/s/Rock%20Chalk%20Weekly/d9963474-d31e-562e-b24a-2108e9feee08/Rock%20Chalk%20Weekly%20Vol%201%20Issue%2024/Cover.html |newspaper=Rock Chalk Weekly |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |publisher=[[Kansas Jayhawks|Kansas Athletics, Inc.]] |volume=1 |issue=24 |access-date=February 18, 2015 }} On May 21, 2014, Mykhailiuk [[National Letter of Intent|committed]] to play basketball at the [[University of Kansas]] and played for the team during their [[2014–15 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2014–2015 season]].{{cite web|title=Kansas adds Ukrainian star Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24569048/kansas-adds-ukrainian-star-sviatoslav-mykhailiuk|work=CBS.com}} During his freshman season, he started five of the first seven games of the season, averaging 21.3 minutes a game, but his playing time since then was significantly curtailed. He scored 11 points while playing 32 minutes in the Orlando Classic Championship game against [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] on November 30, 2014. He was the youngest player in [[Big 12 Conference]] history at 17 years old. Returning to Kansas in his sophomore year Mykhailiuk has averaged 5.4 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.9 assist per game in 35 games of the [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2015-2016 basketball season]], while hitting 40.2% of his three point shots.{{cite news |last= |first= |date= |title=10 Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6589&path=mbball |newspaper=KU Athletics Department |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=April 14, 2016 }}{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=April 12, 2016 |title=Mykhailiuk reveals on Twitter he’s coming back for junior season |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/apr/12/mykhailiuk-reveals-twitter-hes-coming-back/?mens_basketball |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=April 14, 2016 }} On November 23, 2015, Mykhailiuk scored 18 points against [[Chaminade Silverswords|Chaminade University]]. In the first round of the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2016 NCAA basketball tourney]], on March 17, 2016, Mykhailiuk scored 23 points, setting his personal college career scoring record, with 9 of 11 field goals and 4 of 5 threes against the [[2015–16 Austin Peay Governors basketball team|Austin Peay Governors]].{{cite news |last=Keegan |first=Tom |date=March 17, 2016 |title=Svi Mykhailiuk puts on show in first-round blowout |url=http://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/keegan_ratings/2016/mar/17/svi-mykhailiuk-puts-on-show-in-first-rou/ |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=March 25, 2016|quote=Caught fire catching-and-shooting from deep in the corner, dribbled into buckets, got up high on a slam and generally showed off the tools that NBA scouts find intriguing on his way to career-high 23 points (9 of 11 field goals, 4 of 5 threes).}} Mykhailiuk returned to the [[Kansas Jayhawks]] for his junior year in college. On December 22, 2016, in game against [[UNLV]] Mykhailiuk scored 20 points with 6 rebounds, 2 assists, and 2 steals, assisting KU in a 71 to 53 win in [[Las Vegas]].{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=December 22, 2016 |title=Kansas rolls past UNLV in Las Vegas |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article122596084.html |newspaper=The Kansas City Star |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=January 30, 2017 }}{{cite news |last= |first= |date=December 22, 2016 |title=Kansas 71 UNLV 53 |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/boxscore.aspx?id=11998&path=mbball |newspaper=[[University of Kansas]] |location=Lawrence, Kansas |access-date=January 30, 2017 }}{{cite news |last= |first= |date= |title=10 Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7137 |newspaper=[[University of Kansas]] |location=Lawrence, Kansas |access-date=January 30, 2017 }} In the UNLV game, Mykhailiuk made 4 of 6 three point attempts.Keegan, Tom. [http://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/keegan_ratings/2016/dec/22/josh-jackson-moves-to-second-in-season-s/ Josh Jackson moves to second in season standings by putting on first-half show in Vegas], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', December 22, 2016. In the 2016-2017 season, Mykhailiuk has averaged 10.6 points a game, 3.5 rebounds a game, and 1.6 assists per game, while shooting 41.5% from three point territory. On April 12, 2017, Mykhailiuk decided to enter the [[2017 NBA Draft]], but did not hire an agent, allowing him to return for his senior year if he wanted to.{{cite web|title=Mykhailiuk to enter NBA Draft without an agent|url=http://kuathletics.com/news/2017/4/12/mens-basketball-mykhailiuk-to-enter-nba-draft-without-an-agent.aspx?|website=KUAthletics.com}} Mykhailiuk decided to return to Kansas for the [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2017-2018 season]] instead of entering the draft. On November 17, 2017, Mykhailiuk scored a career high 27 points in a game against San Diego State.{{cite web |url=http://m.kusports.com/news/2017/nov/17/svi-mykhailiuk-catches-fire-sparks-blowout-win-ove/?templates.html |title=Svi Mykhailiuk catches fire, sparks blowout win over South Dakota State |last=Chasen |first=Scott |work=KUsports.com |date= November 17, 2017 |access-date= November 19, 2017 }} ===College Stats=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
